text:
# ICD-10-AM Principal Diagnosis: **U07.1 – COVID-19, virus identified**

## Rationale

- **Reason for admission:** The patient was admitted to an isolation centre and treated mainly for COVID-19, with fever, dry cough, dyspnoea, weakness and severe hypoxaemia (SpO₂ 72%). Under ACS 0001 *Principal Diagnosis*, COVID-19 is the condition chiefly responsible for the episode of care.
- **Code choice:** The summary says he was "diagnosed with COVID-19", which implies laboratory confirmation. That supports U07.1 rather than U07.2 (COVID-19, virus not identified).
- **Symptoms are not coded separately:** Fever, cough, dyspnoea and weakness are integral to COVID-19, so they should not be assigned their own codes.

## Possible additional diagnoses (if documentation supports them)

| Condition | Suggested code | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Hypoxaemia / respiratory failure | J96.0x | Code only if the clinician documents respiratory failure; 72% saturation alone is not enough |
| COVID-19 pneumonia | J12.8 | Code only if pneumonia is documented, for example on imaging. Follow current IHACPA/ACS sequencing advice for COVID-19 manifestations |
| Chronic sinusitis | J32.9 | Code if it met ACS 0002 additional diagnosis criteria |
| Hyperglycaemia | R73.9, or E11.x if diabetes is confirmed | Hyperglycaemia needing management meets ACS 0002 |

## Important caveat

This clinical picture (COVID-19 with chronic sinusitis and hyperglycaemia) matches published case series of **COVID-associated mucormycosis**. If the withheld diagnosis section confirms rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis (**B46.1**), the principal diagnosis may change. That would apply if the mucormycosis, rather than COVID-19, was the main reason for admission or treatment. Check the full documentation before finalising the code.
